title_zh: 統合分析：青少年花在社交媒體的時間，與焦慮憂鬱關聯極弱（37 項研究）
title_en: Social media time and teen anxiety depression meta-analysis
summary_zh: 澳洲天主教大學團隊在《British Journal of Clinical Psychology》發表的系統性回顧，綜合 37 項縱貫與實驗研究、近 80,000 名 10 至 24 歲青少年。社交媒體使用時間與其後抑鬱症狀的合併相關係數 r=0.08（12 項研究），焦慮 r=0.093（5 項研究），合共解釋不足 1% 的症狀差異。效應不隨年齡、追蹤期或發表年份改變。作者認為，單靠限制使用時間，未必能解決青少年心理健康危機。
summary_en: An Australian Catholic University systematic review in the British Journal of Clinical Psychology pooled 37 longitudinal and experimental studies of nearly 80,000 young people aged 10-24. Time on social media correlated only very weakly with later symptoms: depression pooled r = .08 (12 studies), anxiety r = .093 (5 studies), together explaining under 1% of symptom variation. Effects did not vary by age, follow-up length or publication year. The authors conclude restricting time alone is unlikely to resolve the youth mental-health crisis.
evidence_note: 系統性回顧與統合分析（British Journal of Clinical Psychology，2026-10-08 線上刊出；DOI: 10.1111/bjc.70100，PMID 42845154）
caution: 37 項研究中有 36 項屬觀察性，不能證明因果；只量度使用時間或頻率，未計內容、社交比較、網絡欺凌或睡眠等因素；結果不等於社交媒體對青少年心理健康無害。
brief_zh: 37 項研究（36 項縱貫觀察、1 項實驗），近 80,000 名 10–24 歲青少年，來自 15 個高收入國家
使用時間合共解釋不足 1% 的焦慮憂鬱症狀差異
效應不隨年齡、追蹤期或發表年份改變
唯一實驗（n=182）：已嚴重抑鬱的青年把使用限於每天 1 小時內，症狀有所減輕
supervision_questions: 家長問「禁手機可唔可以改善個仔嘅情緒」時，你會如何用這份證據回應，同時不否定他們的擔心？

posts.author_name: Peachey et al.（澳洲天主教大學）
posts.title: Social media exposure and anxiety and depression in young people: A systematic review and meta-analysis of longitudinal and experimental studies (Br J Clin Psychol; DOI: 10.1111/bjc.70100)
posts.content: PubMed 摘要：37 項縱貫與實驗研究的系統性回顧與統合分析，含抑鬱與焦慮的合併效應量。

related.title_zh: 瑞典研究：與現實朋友密集網上交流的青少年心理健康較佳，只與網友交流則較差（3,034 人）
related.title_en: Online communication friends and teen well-being Sweden
related.summary_zh: 《Child and Adolescent Mental Health》2026 年 11 月 4 日刊出的合併橫斷面研究，分析瑞典 3,034 名 15 歲青少年（2017/2018 與 2021/2022 年 HBSC 調查），以簡版 Warwick-Edinburgh 心理健康量表（SWEMWBS）量度心理健康。與密友及較大朋友群密集網上交流，與較佳心理健康相關；與只在網上認識的朋友中度或密集交流，則與較差心理健康相關，女童與自覺家庭較不富裕的青少年尤甚。作者指出，重點不只是上網多久，更是與誰交流。
related.summary_en: A pooled cross-sectional study in Child and Adolescent Mental Health (4 November 2026) analysed 3,034 Swedish 15-year-olds from the 2017/2018 and 2021/2022 HBSC surveys, measuring mental well-being with the Short Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Well-being Scale. Intense online communication with close friends and larger friend groups was linked to better well-being, while moderate or intense communication with online-only friends was linked to poorer well-being, especially among girls and adolescents who saw their families as less wealthy. The authors argue what matters is not only time online but who adolescents talk to.

related.title_zh: 研究：青少年在社交媒體上與人比較，與焦慮抑鬱症狀關聯最強
related.title_en: Social comparison on social media strongest link adolescent mental health symptoms
related.summary_zh: Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and Mental Health 於 2026 年 10 月 17 日刊出的橫斷面研究，分析挪威東南部 21 間學校 4,011 名青少年（平均 14 歲，2025 年秋季問卷）。在社交媒體使用五個面向中，「與人比較」對五種症狀的預測力最強：內化症狀（廣泛焦慮、社交焦慮、抑鬱）解釋約 20–26% 變異，外化症狀（ADHD、對立違抗）解釋 6–9%；「消磨時間」與「尋求支持」則幾無獨立關聯。研究不能證明因果關係。
related.summary_en: A cross-sectional study in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and Mental Health (published 17 October 2026) analysed 4,011 Norwegian adolescents (mean age 14) from 21 schools in South-Eastern Norway. Among five aspects of social media use, social comparison was the strongest predictor across all five symptom domains, accounting for about 20-26% of variance in internalizing symptoms (generalized anxiety, social anxiety, depression) and 6-9% in externalizing symptoms (ADHD, oppositional defiant disorder); passing time and seeking support showed negligible independent associations. The design cannot establish causation.

related.title_zh: 英國 16 歲以下社交媒體禁令：教師與神經多樣性顧問的兩種看法
related.title_en: UK under-16 social media ban: two professional perspectives
related.summary_zh: 英國政府於 2026 年 6 月宣布，明年起禁止 16 歲以下使用 YouTube、Instagram 等多個社交平台（WhatsApp、Signal 除外）。教師顧問 Andrew Apraku 以校內網絡欺凌、深偽圖像、睡眠不足等問題支持禁令；自閉症顧問 Ann Memmott 則指出社交媒體是孤立、殘障與神經多樣青少年的重要連結，並引用澳洲經驗指約七成年輕人在數月內找到繞過方法。
related.summary_en: Anna Freud presents two professional views on the UK's planned under-16 social media ban: a teacher who supports it citing cyberbullying and deepfakes, and a neurodiversity consultant who warns it may cut off isolated and neurodivergent youth.
